entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen35831" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen35832" type="x-p"/> This chapter begins with showing the great and free favor which God had manifested to the Israelites, above what he had done to the Edomites, who are threatened with farther marks of the Divine displeasure; alluding, perhaps, to the calamities which they suffered from Judas Maccabeus and John Hyrcanus, (see 1 Maccabees 5:65, and Joseph Antiq. 13:9), <reference osisRef="Mal.1.1-Mal.1.5">Mal 1:1-5</reference>. God then reproaches his people, and especially their priests, for their ungrateful returns to his distinguished goodness, <reference osisRef="Mal.1.6">Mal 1:6</reference>. They are particularly charged with sacrificing the refuse of beasts, <reference osisRef="Mal.1.7-Mal.1.9">Mal 1:7-9</reference>, for which God threatens to reject them, <reference osisRef="Mal.1.10">Mal 1:10</reference>, and choose other nations who will show more reverence to his name and worship, <reference osisRef="Mal.1.11-Mal.1.14">Mal 1:11-14</reference>. <div eID="gen35832" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35833" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen35833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35834" type="x-p"/> The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi - This prophet is undoubtedly the last of the Jewish prophets. He lived after Zechariah and Haggai; for we find that the temple, which was begun in their time, was standing complete in his. See <reference osisRef="Mal.3.10">Mal 3:10</reference>. Some have thought that he was contemporary with Nehemiah; indeed, several have supposed that Malachi, is no other than Ezra under the feigned name of angel of the Lord, or my angel. John the Baptist was the link that connected Malachi with Christ. According to Abp. Usher he flourished b.c. 416, but the authorized version, which we have followed in the margin, states this event to have happened nineteen years later. Both the Hebrew language and poetry had declined in his days. <div eID="gen35834" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35835" type="x-p"/> Israel - Here means the Jewish people in general.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen35835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35836" type="x-p"/> Was not Esau Jacob's brother? - Have I not shown a greater partiality to the Israelites than I have to the Edomites? <div eID="gen35836" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35837" type="x-p"/> I loved Jacob - My love to Jacob has been proved by giving him greater privileges and a better inheritance than what I have given to Esau.
entries.content_plain: Verse 2 Was not Esau Jacob's brother? - Have I not shown a greater partiality to the Israelites than I have to the Edomites? I loved Jacob - My love to Jacob has been proved by giving him greater privileges and a better inheritance than what I have given to Esau.
entries.reader_content_plain: Verse 2 Was not Esau Jacob's brother? - Have I not shown a greater partiality to the Israelites than I have to the Edomites? I loved Jacob - My love to Jacob has been proved by giving him greater privileges and a better inheritance than what I have given to Esau.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen35837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35838" type="x-p"/> And I hated Esau - I have shown him less love; <reference osisRef="Gen.29.30">Gen 29:30</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.29.31">Gen 29:31</reference>. I comparatively hated him by giving him an inferior lot. And now, I have not only laid waste the dwelling-place of the Edomites, by the incursions of their enemies; but (<reference osisRef="Mal.1.4">Mal 1:4</reference>) they shall remain the perpetual monuments of my vengeance. On the subject of loving Jacob and hating Esau, see the notes on Genesis 27 (note), and <reference osisRef="Rom.9.13">Rom 9:13</reference> (note). Let it be remembered, <div eID="gen35838" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35839" type="x-p"/> 1. That there is not a word spoken here concerning the eternal state of either Jacob or Esau. <div eID="gen35839" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35840" type="x-p"/> 2. That what is spoken concerns merely their earthly possessions. And, <div eID="gen35840" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35841" type="x-p"/> 3. That it does not concern the two brothers at all, but the posterity of each.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen35841" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35842" type="x-p"/> They shall build, but I will throw down - We have already seen enough of the wickedness of the Edomites to justify the utmost severity of Divine justice against them. The pulling down predicted here was by Judas Maccabeus; see 1 Maccabees 5:65; and by John Hyrcanus; see Joseph Antiq., lib. 13 c. 9. s. 1. <div eID="gen35842" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35843" type="x-p"/> They shall call them, The border of wickedness - A wicked land. Among this people scarcely any trace of good could ever be noted.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen35849" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35850" type="x-p"/> Beseech God - There were evident marks of God's displeasure in the land, and it was occasioned by these pollutions through the priests. And now he exhorts them to pray to God that they may be pardoned: for, if this practice be persisted in, God will not accept any offering made by them.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen35850" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35851" type="x-p"/> Who is - among you - From this we learn that there was not one sincere or honest priest among them. They were selfish and worldly; and so basely so, that not one of them would even kindle a fire on the hearth of the altar unless he were paid for it.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen35851" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35852" type="x-p"/> From the rising of the sun - The total abolition of the Mosaic sacrifices, and the establishment of a spiritual worship over the whole earth, is here foretold. The incense of praise, and the pure offering of the Lamb without spot, and through him a holy, loving heart, shall be presented everywhere among the Gentiles; and the Jews and their mock offerings shall be rejected.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen35853" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35854" type="x-p"/> Ye have snuffed at it - A metaphor taken from cattle which do not like their fodder. They blow strongly through their nose upon it; and after this neither they nor any other cattle will eat it. <div eID="gen35854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35855" type="x-p"/> Ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick - There had never been such abominations in the Divine worship before. What was of no worth in itself, and what could not be used by its owner, was brought to God's altar, and offered for sacrifice! Was not the punishment of these wretches less than their crimes?

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen35855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35856" type="x-p"/> Cursed be the deceiver - Those who act thus, as they cannot elude God's notice, so neither shall they escape his curse. <div eID="gen35856" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35857" type="x-p"/> And voweth, and sacrificeth - a corrupt thing - The history of Ananias and Sapphira, <reference osisRef="Act.5.1">Act 5:1</reference>, etc., is a complete comment on this. It was high time to break up this corrupt service; and after this time God does not appear to have paid any regard to it, for he sent them no other prophet.  <chapter eID="Mal.1"/> <div eID="gen35857" type="x-p"/>
